Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap is the sweet spot for this game — it feels smooth on the LCD, keeps GPU power reasonable, and the medium settings give the world colour and detail without overwhelming the RDNA 2 GPU. Reduce Unit Size to Small in large multiplayer or siege battles if frame rate dips.

profiles.Summary: Total War: WARHAMMER II runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with a gold ProtonDB rating, meaning most players get it working well with minor tweaks. The game is CPU-intensive during turn processing and real-time battles with large armies, so expect some frame dips in the most demanding encounters even at lower settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (the Deck's GPU sits between the minimum GTX 460 and recommended GTX 770), the game's known CPU sensitivity, and the Deck hardware profile. On your first run, check frame rates during a mid-game real-time battle with large armies — that is the most demanding scenario — and drop to Optimal or Max Battery if it struggles.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps GPU load low enough for a meaningful battery saving. AI turn times are unaffected by these settings — expect brief pauses during late-game campaigns.

KnownIssues: Turn-end processing (AI turns) can cause brief stalls regardless of GPU settings, as it is CPU-bound
No native Linux build; runs via Proton — occasional compatibility quirks may require selecting a specific Proton version
Large late-game battles with many units can push frame rates below 30 fps even at low settings
On-screen text and UI elements may be small at 1280x800; the game's UI scaling options help but may not fully resolve readability

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high settings the GPU is pushed hard; 60 fps is achievable in campaign and smaller battles but large real-time engagements will drop to the low 40s. Shadow Quality is kept at Medium as Ultra shadows are disproportionately expensive on this GPU.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap delivers a smooth, tear-free experience that the Deck's OLED handles well. Campaign map will run comfortably above 40 fps; expect the cap to be tested in very large battles.
